subject: Error when running micro_terra with microclima parameter & seeking advice on parameter optimization

messages.author: 9c4f6174918792db
messages.subject: Error when running micro_terra with microclima parameter & seeking advice on parameter optimization
parts:
Hi all,

I have been working with the micro_terra() function to model microclimate temperatures. My workflow involves sampling coordinates across several different study area polygons (which ranging from 12km² to 3,000,000 km²) and aggregating hourly temperatures into averages for the hottest days over study periods of 1-5 decades. (I will also be feeding the microclimate outputs into the ectotherm model for a few species). My goal is to get temperature estimates that may better reflect extreme temperature exposure of species compared to air temperatures 1-2 meters above land. 

I encountered an error while experimenting with parameters and also had a question about optimizing the model inputs for global scale studies

1. Error when using microclima = 1 with timeinterval = 365. I am attempting to get daily maximum temperatures from the hourly output.

    > micro <- micro_terra(timeinterval = 365, microclima = 1)
    If program is crashing, try run.gads = 2.

    extracting wind speed data from TerraClimate

    extracting vapour pressure deficit data from TerraClimate

    extracting solar radiation data from TerraClimate

    extracting soil moisture data from TerraClimate
    running micro_global to get clear sky solar
    If program is crashing, try run.gads = 2.

    extracting climate data

    extracting soil moisture data
    running microclimate model for 365 days by 1 years at site long -89.4557 lat 43.1379

    Note: the output column `SOLR` in metout and shadmet is for unshaded horizontal plane solar radiation

    runtime 0.101000000000113 seconds
    using microclima and elevatr to adjust solar for topographic and vegetation effects
    Downloading digital elevation data
     Accessing raster elevation [=========================] 100%
    Mosaicing & Projecting
    running microclimate model, splining monthly data to daily, for 2000 to  2015 at site long -89.4557 lat 43.1379

    Note: the output column `SOLR` in metout and shadmet is for unshaded horizontal plane solar radiation

    runtime 11.049 seconds
    Error in micro_terra(timeinterval = 365, microclima = 1) :
      object 'diffuse_frac' not found




2. I am currently working on the following parameter combination to model microclimates.
    micro <- micro_terra(
        loc = current_coords,
        ystart = start_year,
        yfinish = end_year,
        timeinterval = 365,
        elevatr = 1,
        terrain = 1)

I was wondering if there are any recommendations on parameter settings for large scale studies to maximize accuracy without overcomplicating the model. Any suggestions or guidance would be very appreciated.

Thank you!

Neha :)

messages.author: 6cec8ea3702ece93
messages.subject: Re: Error when running micro_terra with microclima parameter & seeking advice on parameter optimization
parts:
Dear Neha,

First, thanks for spotting the error. You appear to be the first person to try running micro_terra with microclima = 1 and timeinterval = 365. It was an easy fix and is now in the latest push to github.

For the second question, it is hard to advise without knowing more about what you are trying to do. If you want to capture exposure to hot weather conditions, you'd be better to use micro_era5 or micro_ncep (global) or micro_usa (USA-specific) or micro_silo (Australia-specific) because they use hourly or daily weather. The micro_terra uses monthly averages. But micro_terra will give you a good estimate of how much hotter it is close to the ground compared to at weather station height. If you are concerned about soil moisture or terrain effects, then you might want to start changing parameters from defaults to e.g. match soil hydraulic properties, hill shade and slope/aspect in rugged terrain.

Hope that helps,
Mike
